scope: XDG paths, HOME fallback, relative overrides, foreign CWD independence and config selection (src/settings/paths.ts, src/settings/load.ts, src/cli.ts config selection/reporting, src/config.ts db default, scripts/smoke.ts config entry, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/ENVIRONMENT.md)

findings.title: Relative HOME bypasses the absolute-path guard: default config and database paths become working-directory relative
findings.evidence: homeDirectory() rejects a non-absolute HOME at paths.ts:15-18, then falls through to `return normalize(homedir())` at paths.ts:19. On POSIX os.homedir() returns $HOME verbatim when it is set, including a relative value, so the fallback reintroduces exactly the rejected value (confirmed on Bun 1.3.14, Bun 1.4.2 and Node). defaultConfigPath/defaultDatabasePath (paths.ts:57-73) then return relative paths, load.ts:739-741 uses defaultConfigPath(env) unanchored, and load.ts:835-841 passes the relative database path through unchanged; src/store.ts:19 mkdirSync(dirname(path)) plus new Database(path) resolve against process.cwd(). This contradicts docs/CONFIGURATION.md:21-24, which states a checkout cannot change a service's configuration. Local probe with a relative HOME: homeDirectory returned a relative path; defaultConfigPath returned a relative config path; resolveServerSettings with an unrelated cwd option still selected the file in process.cwd(); the resolved SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH was relative and constructing a Store created the directory inside process.cwd(); CLI `config path` printed the relative path with exists:true and `serve --check-config` returned ok:true. Tilde expansion is also wrong: a tilde host_path resolves to <base>/<relative home>/<name> instead of an absolute home path.
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone at /tmp/rev35/probe-copy; fixture planted under /tmp/rev35/repro; run from that directory with a relative HOME: (1) homeDirectory returns a relative path; (2) resolveServerSettings({env, cwd: unrelated}) selects the planted relative config file because readFile resolves it against process.cwd(); (3) resolved db path is relative and Store() creates the tree in the CWD; (4) CLI config path / serve --check-config report the relative config path. Log: /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rev35-f1-repro.log
findings.recommendation: Validate the os.homedir() fallback with isAbsolute too and fail closed with a SettingsError (or resolve the real account home independently of $HOME) instead of returning a relative value; defensively reject or re-anchor relative default config/database paths in load.ts.

findings.title: `config path` reports the invocation directory as an existing config file for an empty --config, diverging from the resolver
findings.evidence: configPath() at cli.ts:215-224 duplicates the selection logic of prepare()/selector() in src/settings/load.ts. anchorPath with an empty string resolves to the invocation directory, so `config path --config ""` prints that directory with exists:true and exit 0, while the resolver treats the same empty configPath as an explicit selection and fails config_invalid (EISDIR); `serve --check-config` and `config validate` exit 1.
findings.reproduction: HOME=<tmp> bun src/cli.ts config path --config "" -> config_path = CWD, exists = true, exit 0; HOME=<tmp> bun src/cli.ts serve --check-config --config "" -> EISDIR, exit 1. Log: /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rev35-f1-repro.log
findings.recommendation: Treat an empty --config / SWARMFORGE_CONFIG as unset in both code paths (selector() already skips it), or reject it as a usage error in src/cli/arguments.ts value(); preferably have configPath() reuse the resolver's selection helper so reporting cannot drift from resolution.

findings.title: scripts/smoke.ts bypasses the settings resolver and ignores config file, env_file and XDG defaults
findings.evidence: smoke() calls loadConfig() directly (scripts/smoke.ts:18), unlike src/main.ts:7 and src/cli.ts:194 which call resolveServerSettings. loadConfig() reads process.env only and applies the schema default SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH = './data/swarmforge.sqlite' (src/config.ts:77), so it ignores SWARMFORGE_CONFIG, the discovered config file, the config file's env_file and the XDG database default. Verified locally: with a valid config file declaring an absolute server.db_path plus env_file, resolveServerSettings returned that absolute path while loadConfig returned the CWD-relative default, and running the script with the opt-in variable aborted on missing provider/model values even though the config file and its env file supplied them.
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone with HOME=<tmp> and <tmp>/.config/swarmforge/config.toml declaring schema_version=1, env_file and an absolute server.db_path: resolveServerSettings -> that absolute db_path; loadConfig -> the CWD-relative default; running the script aborts although the config file plus env file supply the required values. Log: /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rev35-f1-repro.log
findings.recommendation: Resolve the smoke script's configuration through resolveServerSettings({ env: process.env }) so it exercises the same entry point as serve, and add a test asserting the script's resolved SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH matches the resolver for the same environment.
